title: Sometimes the straw is the whole trick.
summary: A genuine kitchen-counter discovery with INTENSE strawberry milk from Wegmans: preferred straws, safer lid options, and printable picture communication prompts.
search: Home / Journal / Little Things That Help The family notebook · Little Things That Help · No. 01 Sometimes the straw is the whole trick. A familiar drink, a bendy straw, and one less thing to wrestle with. Some of our most useful discoveries begin at the kitchen counter, not in an aisle full of clever gadgets. This one involved a bottle of INTENSE® Lowfat Strawberry Milk we picked up at Wegmans, and the simple preference for a straw. See what we tried ↓ Original family photograph, gently brightened and sharpened. The product and scene are unchanged. A small domestic discoveryKeep the familiar thing. Change the fiddly part. The milk was familiar. The straw was familiar. The awkward part was keeping the straw where it belonged while using the bottle. A tiny adjustment to the setup made the idea worth photographing. Our first kitchen experiment used an opening in the bottle cap to hold a bendy straw. It was a quick test, not a product recommendation or a how-to for cutting drink lids. If we were setting this up for daily use, we would look for a compatible, food-safe straw lid or pour the drink into a clean reusable cup with its own fitted lid. Cut plastic can leave sharp edges or loose pieces. The real lesson is pleasantly ordinary: sometimes you don't need to change someone's preferred drink, cup, or routine. You just need to find a way to make it easier to use. The bottle and its cap, before the straw. The cap detail from our first test. From our family camera rollThe little detail we wanted to remember.These photographs record a one-off experiment, not instructions to cut plastic caps. For daily use, we would choose a compatible, purpose-made food-safe straw lid or a clean reusable cup with a secure lid.Check that the lid and straw fit securely, have smooth intact surfaces, and are clean. Discard damaged parts. If someone has swallowing precautions, use the drinking setup recommended by their care team. The useful part, in fullThree things to remember. Start with what works.A familiar flavor and a preferred straw can be more important than buying another new cup. Choose a secure, smooth lid.A compatible, food-safe straw top or reusable lidded cup is a better repeatable choice than a hand-cut cap. Keep milk cold.Follow the bottle's refrigeration directions, clean reusable parts and never keep a cap with loose or sharp plastic. For the communication toolkit A picture for the preference. Sometimes it helps to separate the choices: the drink, and the way someone wants to drink it. We sketched two simple prompts—STRAWBERRY MILK with a little watercolor strawberry beside the bottle, and STRAW—for families who find visual supports useful. Print them, or use the idea to add a familiar photograph and preferred words to an existing AAC system. A picture of the actual bottle may be easier to recognize than an illustration. Open printable picture cards ↗Make a card with your own photo → Original editorial sketches, not official PECS symbols or a substitute for individualized communication support. Use the words and symbols a person already understands. Strawberry milk or straw, with a little watercolor berry to make the drink easy to recognize. The drink in our photographsIntense® Lowfat Strawberry Milk Bought at Wegmans: This is the 16-ounce strawberry milk shown in our own family snapshots, made by Upstate Niagara Cooperative. You can see the Wegmans listing or visit the brand below. The bottle prompted the idea; the tip isn't an endorsement of a particular drinking setup. Independent family-life note. Not sponsored, gifted or an affiliate link. Visit the official product page ↗ Why we keep these little notes The package is part of the experience. For some families, the useful detail isn't just what tastes good. It's how a bottle opens, whether a favorite straw fits, how easily the drink can be offered, and whether someone can ask for it in their own way. Those small details deserve a place in an everyday product conversation. Retailers, makers, clinicians and fellow families are welcome to share a link to this independent family note. Please ask before reproducing our photographs or original picture cards. We purchased the milk ourselves; this is not a paid feature. title: The lovely part and the useful part.
summary: An AUsome Life media kit: published travel stories, original family photography, proposed coverage and a practical autism and access perspective.
search: Media kit · press · partnerships The lovely part and the useful part. An AUsome Life is a Massachusetts-based New England family-life publication about places worth going, things worth buying twice, and the practical details that help a family actually participate. We can care about a beautiful hotel room and whether the pool setup works. A good sweater and whether it survives real life. A lovely dinner and the plan that gets everybody there. High-support autism is part of our family life, not the only thing worth talking about. Download press release (.txt)View media kit MASSACHUSETTS, October 4, 2026 — An AUsome Life, a Massachusetts-based New England family-life publication, today announced the launch of its website at anausomelife.com. Building on the family’s existing Instagram account, the site brings outings, travel, home, classic style and useful everyday products together with a perspective shaped by raising an autistic teen with very high support needs. The publication looks at what makes a good day possible: a warm hotel pool, a quieter place to pause, clothes that feel right, food that works for the family and enough information to decide whether an outing is worth the drive. Its New England sensibility makes room for both an elegant coastal visit and an ordinary grocery run. Readers can explore family field notes, favorite places, practical guides and planning tools. Coverage connects the appealing parts of a destination or product with the details that often determine whether it works in everyday life, including pacing, comfort, cleanup, cost and the option to leave early. Profound autism advocacy is part of that editorial foundation. An AUsome Life addresses significant support needs plainly while keeping the person’s age, preferences and dignity in view. Its approach to universal design asks how clearer information, easier routines and more usable places and products can help a wider range of people participate. The site welcomes readers looking for good New England places, practical purchases and a more manageable family day, including parents, caregivers, extended family and people who simply appreciate useful details. Personal experience remains identified as one family’s experience, with reported information and future editorial plans distinguished from completed visits and hands-on reviews. The publication’s editorial standards call for clear disclosure of gifted, hosted, paid and affiliate relationships. A product or stay does not purchase a positive verdict. Journalists, destinations and brands can find editorial information and contact details in the media kit. Visit anausomelife.com and follow @anausomelife on Instagram. About An AUsome Life An AUsome Life is a Massachusetts-based family-life publication. It covers New England outings and travel, home, classic style, useful products and profound autism advocacy, with a focus on everyday participation and the practical details that help families make their own choices.
